muse_spark_1.3/001: The strategy is short path control with exact tactical cover. Black needs top-bottom, White left-right. The cost of a cell is 0 for own, 1 for empty, blocked for opponent and the virtual-connection distance is the number of empties needed to connect, computed by 0-1 BFS with early exit on first target pop. Current distances tell if there is a one-move win. All wins are tested by flood fill through own stones only. Otherwise every empty is tried: `score = oppDist - myDist` plus a tiny central / adjacency tie breaker. Moves are sorted and re-searched 2-ply: my candidate vs opponent best reply in that set, with alpha-beta cutoffs and time guard. Best worst-case move is played, guaranteeing legal play, immediate win, immediate block, greedy short-path play and 2-ply refutation defence.
muse_spark_1.3/002: Strategy is Dijkstra shortest-path control with 2-ply minimax. Cost is 0 for own stone, 1 for empty, blocked for opponent stone, connecting opposite sides. 1-ply evaluates every empty by `opp_dist - my_dist` after the move to rank candidates and find immediate wins. Top ~10-12 candidates are searched to depth 2: my move then opponent best reply minimizing the same score, with alpha-beta pruning and centrality/connection tie-break. This blocks imminent threats, preserves virtual connections, and attacks simultaneously, all within ~400 Dijkstras on 11x11 which is well under 1s. Opening plays center.
muse_spark_1.3/003: The strategy is Dijkstra shortest-path evaluation with 2-ply minimax. Empty cells cost 1, own stones cost 0, opponent stones are blocked. The minimum cost to connect the two sides is the number of stones needed to win. Playing a move reduces own cost and increases opponent cost by blocking. All moves are scored by `opp_dist - my_dist` after the move, immediate wins and must-blocks are handled tactically, the best moves are re-searched with opponent best reply minimax, centre and connection tie-breakers are added.
muse_spark_1.3/004:
The strategy is Dijkstra shortest-path Hex evaluation with 2-ply
interdiction search. Empty costs 1, own stones 0, opponent stones
blocked, 0-1 BFS gives number of empties needed to connect.
Immediate win is distance 0, immediate threat is distance 1.
Otherwise every empty is scored by 1-ply `OppDist-MeDist` after
playing there, top moves are re-searched by letting the opponent
reply on the union of the two shortest paths and maximin-ing the
leaf difference. Center bias breaks ties. This finds wins,
blocks losses, attacks and defends the shortest virtual connections.
muse_spark_1.3/005: The strategy is shortest-path control with 2-ply tactical search. Black connects top-bottom, White left-right. Cost of a cell is 0 for own stone, 1 for empty, blocked for opponent, so Dijkstra 0-1 shortest path equals stones needed to connect. Central opening, immediate win, immediate block, then 1-ply evaluation of every empty by simulating own attack `D_me(m)` and opponent block `D_opp_block(m)` with score `D_opp_block - D_me`. Tie break by start/end distance potentials, centrality and adjacency. Top candidates are verified by 2-ply minimax where value is `D_opp - D_me` and opponent minimizes, which catches ladders, bridges and double threats. All search uses heap Dijkstra with early exit and time guard, always returning a legal move.
